A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dream-MPC study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material in Appendices A–F and identifying the new Appendix G.

before.justification: v1 reports original continuous-control experiments, learning curves, benchmark comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses of planner gradients and model exploitation.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds an uncertainty-regularization ablation and empirical analyses of value estimation and policy mismatch on Dog Run.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same policy initialization, gradient optimization, action reuse, and uncertainty-regularized objective. The five-Q-network BMPC configuration in Appendix G serves as an experimental control for the added analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 24 state-based control tasks, six visual-control tasks, four Dreamer-integration tasks, and Pendulum-v1 gradient tests. Appendix G investigates the existing Dog Run task without introducing another environment or task requirement.

E2.justification: The trained-BMPC comparison gains a 'w/o uncertainty reg.' variant in v3 Table 4, compared with v1 Table 5. Appendix G also compares TD-MPC2 trained with and without MPC. The main benchmark and Dreamer-integration baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces dedicated diagnostic protocols: value estimation using 100 evaluation episodes, quartile-binned error analysis, a BMPC control using five Q-networks instead of two V-networks, and evaluating different critics on BMPC-policy trajectories. These add controlled evaluation designs; the original benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix G examines value calibration throughout training, relationships among critic disagreement, value errors and returns, and policy mismatch on Dog Run. Table 4 additionally ablates uncertainty regularization during trained-BMPC evaluation, complementing the previously reported training ablations and sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Table 19 introduces Spearman correlation analysis and states that all p-values are much smaller than 0.05, while omitting exact values. Existing three-seed, standard-deviation and 95% confidence-interval reporting remains; the PDFs do not establish an increase in training seeds.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values in Tables 11–16 are retained. New Table 4 reports Button Press success of 1.00±0.00 without regularization versus 0.67±0.47 for the full method. Appendix G adds value-calibration findings and nine correlations, including uncertainty–return coefficients of -0.93, -0.88 and -0.80 for policy-only, MPPI and Dream-MPC under the five-Q BMPC setup.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical formulation and Equations 1–17 are retained. Appendix G adds empirical diagnostics and interpretations, without new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about gradient-based planning, policy improvement, computational efficiency, uncertainty regularization and action reuse. The added diagnostics support and qualify existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v1 tentatively attributes weaker high-dimensional training performance to premature convergence. v3 develops an extensive explanation involving exploration, policy mismatch and critic calibration, links smaller regularization benefits to BMPC's smaller value errors, and proposes possible offline-RL applicability. Section 5.3 also strengthens its causal wording about insufficient exploration.

D1.justification: The abstract now reports code and videos as available instead of promising a future release. Table 18 newly specifies Grad-MPC's 0.05 action-optimization rate and explicitly assigns shared PlaNet settings to it. These are additional disclosures, without evidence that the existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Appendix G adds a substantive comparison with Lin et al.'s value-overestimation account, reporting a smaller gap that changes to underestimation during training. The cited-work membership and principal novelty positioning remain stable; Lin's 2025-to-2026 reference update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording corrections, conference front matter, updated cross-references, a new C.3 subsection, and reordering Appendix D. Most existing explanatory prose and the main narrative remain intact; the substantial new material primarily documents Appendix G's scientific analysis.

P2.justification: v3 adds three diagnostic figures and Table 19, expands the ablation table, and enlarges and regroups Table 18. It also relocates the planning-hyperparameter table and planner sweep, redistributes existing appendix figures, and corrects Figure 4's caption to identify all three represented domains.

improvement.justification: The new Dog Run diagnostics and evaluation-time ablation provide useful evidence for a failure mode that v1 explained mainly through speculation. Expanded implementation disclosures also improve reproducibility information. The overall gain is limited: the diagnostic evidence concerns one task with modified BMPC critics, and the stronger causal explanation of insufficient exploration remains only partially established.
